correctness.rationale: Single-cycle successor permutations exactly characterize binary de Bruijn cycles. Cross-join adjacency is two interior truth-table changes. Pairwise-intersecting 2-subsets yield an all-order upper bound. At n=5 all 65536 tables were enumerated; 2048 were valid. The exact rooted extremal count 224 gives 224/14=16 distinct maximum cliques. An independent enumeration by Euler tours and independent maximal-clique enumeration using direct cyclic six-mer intersections give the same set of 16 cliques. The embedded standard-library checker was run successfully.

evidence: Alhakim (2018), Section 2, Table 1: all order-five vertex degrees; Sections 4-5: connectedness and Hamiltonian paths.
Ezerman–Fahreza–Szmidt (2018): all order-five truth-table-distance perturbation patterns, not mutual adjacency among entire candidate cliques.
Dąbrowski–Rachwalik–Szmidt (2026): abstract and indexed description of cross-join algorithms and Fryers polynomials; full article fetch was limited.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A complete degree distribution or full family of single-base perturbation-distance polynomials is weaker than the family of induced clique edge relations. The general graph-theoretic connectivity theorem applies to a different invariant and does not establish the clique count.

originality.rationale: Relevant primary literature establishes connectivity and Hamiltonian paths of cross-join graphs, complete order-five degree frequencies and perturbation-distance patterns. The new theorem compares simultaneous pairwise adjacencies and classifies maximum complete subgraphs; degree sequences and one-source distance distributions do not determine such cliques. No directly covering clique theorem was found in reviewed relevant material. The complete 11-page 2013 archival manuscript was inspected in its available extracted text; no complete-subgraph theorem was present. Unindexed prior work remains a material historical risk.
residual_risks: The later 2026 publisher full text was not fully inspected after an HTTP 429 response. The 2013 open-access PDF extracted text was inspected; page images could not be retrieved (HTTP 403).
A combinatorial equivalence using interlacement or Euler-tour transition systems could produce the same extremal-clique count in unindexed literature.
No independent historical priority certification has been obtained.

value.rationale: For the natural cross-join reconfiguration graph, maximum cliques measure families of cycles mutually one operation apart. The general upper bound is a structural theorem, and the first nontrivial large order saturates it in exactly 16 distinct configurations. The complete natural extremal classification adds simultaneous-adjacency information not captured by existing one-vertex degree counts. The finite count is independently enumerated and not an arbitrary parameter slice.
